recipes.title: Advance egg Omelette
ingredients: 3 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)
1/2 Tbsp sugar (up to 1 Tbsp for a sweeter tamagoyaki)
1 tsp usukuchi (light-colored) soy sauce (or regular soy sauce)
1 Tbsp water (optional, for a fluffier omelette)
For cooking: 1 Tbsp neutral oil (plus more if needed)
steps: Gather all the ingredients. Can be made with a tamagoyaki pan or a carbon steel frying pan (a nonstick pan is easier).
Beat the eggs with the sugar, salt, soy sauce, and water.
Oil the pan, pour in a thin layer of egg, and as it sets roll it up; repeat with more egg, rolling each new layer onto the previous, until all the egg is used.

recipes.title: Egg omelette
ingredients: 3 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)
For cooking: 1 1/2 sheets nori (dried laver seaweed), optional
steps: Beat the eggs with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce, mirin, and salt.
Oil the pan and cook the egg in thin layers, rolling each layer up as it sets (optionally layering in nori).
Serve with grated daikon radish and soy sauce.

recipes.title: Ajitama
recipes.description: Soy-marinated soft-boiled eggs. After 4 days, need to be removed from the sauce or else it's too much (too salty).
steps: Boil the eggs (6:30 gives a runny yolk that takes 4 days to become jelly).
Mix soy sauce + dark soy sauce to be less salty.
Marinate the eggs in the sauce.
Remove from the sauce after 4 days so it doesn't get too salty.
Notes - 6:30 heated in pot: okay, not the best. 7 min: used brown sugar, did not heat up. Test 2: 12 eggs, 4/6 tsp sugar, 3/4 cup soy sauce, 3/4 cup mirin.

recipes.title: Steam Egg
steps: Mix egg and water 1:1, then use a colander/strainer to remove suds and bubbles.
Can season shrimp and add to the egg.
Saran wrap the plate before steaming for a smooth surface.
Steam the egg on high for 4 min, then close the cover for 5 min.
